claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you claiming Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?**

This is important because Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in qualifying education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and is working now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me just check the official guidance to ensure I give you accurate information about Alex's situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official guidance, I now have the information I need to assess Alex's eligibility.

Since Alex is 17 years old, has finished school, is not in any approved education or training, and is now working, there are specific rules that apply:

**Child Benefit stops when a child aged 16 or over:**
- Starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training
- Is not in approved education or training

I have one more question to clarify the situation: **Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

This is relevant because Child Benefit can sometimes continue for 20 weeks for 16 or 17 year olds who leave education/training and register with one of these services.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed services. He just went straight into work after leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make a decision about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Alex is 17 years old** and has left school
- He is **not in approved education or training**
- He has **not registered** with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He has **gone straight into work**

Under the Child Benefit rules, you can normally only continue to receive Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they remain in approved education or training. Child Benefit also stops if a child starts paid work (24 hours or more a week) and is no longer in approved education or training.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he decides to return to approved education or training—you may become eligible again at that point.

If you have any questions or think there may be other circumstances I haven't considered, please feel free to contact the Child Benefit Office directly for further guidance.
